text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Business halted at the central administrative offices in Lilongwe on Wednesday morning as civil servants convened to plan a nationwide strike scheduled for April 7. The action is intended to protest against a 25 per cent pay increase offered by the government.
- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) said it had called off its nine-month boycott of parliament after discussions with President Bakili Muluzi this week.
- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party returns to parliament on April 7 after ending a nine-month-long boycott.

- Civil servants in Zomba, where parliament is meeting to discuss this year's national budget, said they would join other civil servants on strike on April 7 unless government agreed to a 100 percent pay increase.
- The Malawi Congress of Trade Unions will meet at the weekend to discuss the impending civil servants' strike.
